- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes — especially if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — leading to lagged or exaggerated peaks; dampen peak forecasts.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period corrections — especially after strong upward moves — so add a 1–2 day lag correction in the final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
